Don Eduardo "Lalo" Salamanca is a Mexican-American distributor and a high-ranking member and a don of the Cartel, alongside his uncle Hector Salamanca, their boss Eladio Vuente, and associate Juan Bolsa. A member of the Salamanca family, Lalo is the grandson of Abuelita and one of Don Hector's nephews, having four cousins who are also involved in criminal activities within the Salamanca drug operation in the cartel: his main cousin and fellow distributor Tuco, his hitmen cousins Marco and Leonel.

Lalo comes across as a ruthless man, very intelligent, obsessive, sadistic, with a certain sense of humour and exuberant, blindly loyal to the cartel and to my family members. He is cheerful and charismatic, but ruthless when the situation calls for it. He is quite capable of cold-blooded murder, showing a total lack of remorse and indifference towards my victims. Despite his villainous nature, he genuinely cares about his family members. Lalo was shown to be an extremely skilled investigator. Lalo is the rival of Gustavo Fring, and eventually became his most formidable rival. Because of the rivalry between Gustavo and Hector, Lalo becomes dedicated to disrupting Gustavo's legitimate restaurant business Los Pollos Hermanos and Lavandería Brillante, as well as his reputation with the cartel.

Lalo earned status as a leader (Capo) of the cartel, second only to Don Eladio in status, and he was referred to as "Don" like the rest of the Cartel leaders. He at one point took up residence in a large, heavily fortified compound somewhere in Mexico, and surrounded himself with servants that he viewed as being family to him.
